Container.Name: OpenCloud
Container.Overview:
OpenCloud - a modern, self-hosted file sync and share platform (a lightweight OpenCloud/ownCloud-family server) - packaged as a genuine one-click Unraid app. The official OpenCloud image has no PUID/PGID support and needs a manual init step, so a fresh install normally fails with "permission denied". This wrapper fixes that: it runs the one-time init for you, heals the appdata permissions and runs as your chosen PUID/PGID (99/100 = nobody/users by default).
What's pre-configured: • One-click: auto-runs 'opencloud init' on first boot, then the server - nothing to do on the console. • Permission heal: root-created appdata folders are handed to your PUID/PGID automatically. • Serves HTTPS itself on port 9200 (self-signed by default) - no reverse proxy required. • Two channels via the Repository tag: :rolling (default, newest features) and :latest (stable/production). Both track OpenCloud's own upstream release automatically, no manual version bump needed.
Getting started: • Set an Admin Password below - it is applied on the first start. Log in as user "admin". • FIRST START takes a moment: the container generates its config and a self-signed certificate. Wait for the "OPENCLOUD IS READY" banner in the container log, then open the WebUI. • Open the WebUI at https://[IP]:9200 and accept the self-signed certificate once.
Notes: • Public URL: Unraid does NOT auto-fill the "Public URL" field. Set it to https://YOUR-SERVER-IP:9200 (your Unraid LAN IP), or your external https URL behind a reverse proxy. Leaving the placeholder lets the container guess its own IP so it still starts, but client logins only work reliably once it is correct. • Storage driver: keep it on 'posix' (the default). A blank driver or the unsupported 'local' driver makes files show up but stay greyed out (not openable/downloadable). The Data folder must sit on a filesystem with extended-attribute support - the Unraid array and cache/pool disks have it; if files stay greyed out on an exotic share, move Data to a normal appdata/cache-backed path. • Use a FRESH, empty Data folder. Do NOT point Data at an old OpenCloud/oCIS data directory: the on-disk layout differs between versions and the storage backends (local vs S3) are not interchangeable, so the server crash-loops (symptom in the log: search 'cannot open index, metadata missing'). There is no in-place migration between storage backends - to keep old files, start fresh and re-upload them. • Why rolling is the default: OpenCloud's production line is currently 7.2.x, where a single transient NATS timeout ends the whole server process. Slow storage is exactly what produces those timeouts, so the risk is real on an array-backed setup. Rolling carries the fix from 7.5.0 onwards. Production releases about every six months, so the stable line will not pick it up for a while. • Production channel: change the Repository tag from ':rolling' to ':latest' if you prefer OpenCloud's fully QA'd line over the newest features. Keep your appdata backed up before switching either way. • Reverse proxy: if you terminate TLS in front of OpenCloud, set "OpenCloud terminates TLS" to 'false' (advanced) and set the Public URL to your external https URL (e.g. https://cloud.example.com). Then "Allow self-signed TLS" can be 'false'. Your proxy must connect to the container over plain HTTP on port 9200 (not HTTPS) once "OpenCloud terminates TLS" is 'false'. • PUID/PGID default to 99/100 (nobody/users on Unraid).
S3 object storage (optional, advanced): • OpenCloud can store file BLOBS in any S3-compatible bucket. Two genuine, actively-maintained self-hosted options: SeaweedFS (https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/unraid-apps/tree/main/seaweedfs, recommended for a single node) and Garage (https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/garage, built for multi-node clusters, runs single-node here too). AWS, Backblaze B2 and Wasabi also work. Set the "Storage driver" to 'decomposeds3' and fill the S3 endpoint / region / access key / secret key / bucket fields. Keep the driver on 'posix' (the default) for normal local storage - do NOT leave it blank. • IMPORTANT: only the file blobs go to S3. The file-tree METADATA always stays on the local Data volume - so that volume is required even with S3 and MUST be backed up. Losing it orphans your S3 objects (they are opaque IDs with no folder structure). • OpenCloud does NOT use a database (no MySQL/Postgres) - do not look for one. State lives in the local metadata tree plus an embedded message bus.
How to get the S3 bucket and keys: • SeaweedFS (self-hosted): in that template, set an Access Key and Secret Key (see its README's Security note) and optionally a Pre-create Bucket name - those become your access key, secret key and bucket directly, no separate service-account step. Endpoint is its S3 port, http://SEAWEEDFS-IP:8333, region 'default'. • Garage (self-hosted): in that template, set an Access Key and Secret Key (and optionally a Bucket) - pre-seeded on first boot, no separate CLI step. Endpoint is its S3 API port, http://GARAGE-IP:3900, region 'garage'. • AWS S3 / Backblaze B2 / Wasabi: create a bucket in the provider console, then create an access key (AWS: IAM access key; B2/Wasabi: an application/API key). Use the provider's https endpoint and the bucket's region. • If uploads fail with a checksum error on a non-AWS endpoint, add STORAGE_USERS_DECOMPOSEDS3_PUT_OBJECT_DISABLE_CONTENT_SHA256=true as an extra variable.
Source on GitHub: https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/opencloud This is an independent, community-maintained packaging of OpenCloud and is not affiliated with OpenCloud GmbH.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: HTTPS port of the OpenCloud WebUI / API (self-signed cert by default). Open https://[IP]:9200 and accept the certificate once.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Persistent OpenCloud configuration (opencloud.yaml + generated secrets). Created and initialised on first start.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Persistent OpenCloud data: file-tree metadata, the search index, the internal NATS message bus and transient upload staging (plus the file blobs, unless you use an S3/decomposeds3 backend). IMPORTANT: this volume is fsync-heavy, so keep it on a FAST SSD/NVMe pool. The default appdata path is fine only if your appdata is cache-backed (the usual Unraid setup); do NOT point it at the array or a slow /mnt/user share, or large-folder syncs from the desktop client will stall and abort (upstream issue #3027). With decomposeds3/S3 only this small metadata volume needs to be fast; the file blobs go to your S3 bucket, so this stays small and does not grow with file size (only with file count).

Config.Name: Admin Password
Config.Description: Password for the built-in 'admin' user. REQUIRED. Applied on the first start (during init). Choose a strong value - this is the login for your whole cloud.

Config.Name: Public URL
Config.Description: REQUIRED. The URL clients use to reach OpenCloud, and the login (OIDC) issuer. Unraid does NOT auto-fill this: replace YOUR-SERVER-IP with your Unraid server's LAN IP, e.g. https://192.168.1.10:9200 (keep the https:// and the :9200 port). Behind a reverse proxy set your external https URL instead, e.g. https://cloud.example.com. Must be https. If you leave the placeholder, the container falls back to its own IP so it still boots, but client logins may not work until you set the real address.

Config.Name: Allow self-signed TLS
Config.Description: 'true' (default) accepts the container's self-signed certificate - correct for a direct Unraid install. Set 'false' when a reverse proxy provides a valid certificate.

Config.Name: Log Level
Config.Description: Verbosity of the container log.

Config.Name: Create Demo Users
Config.Description: 'true' seeds a set of demo users (alan, mary, ...) with well-known passwords - handy for testing, unsafe for real use. Keep 'false' for a real deployment.

Config.Name: OpenCloud terminates TLS
Config.Description: 'true' (default) = OpenCloud serves HTTPS itself on 9200 (self-signed) - correct for a direct Unraid install. Set 'false' when a reverse proxy terminates TLS in front of the container; then also set the Public URL to your external https URL and 'Allow self-signed TLS' to 'false'.

Config.Name: User ID
Config.Description: User-ID OpenCloud runs as. Default 99 (nobody on Unraid). The wrapper heals appdata ownership to match on start.

Config.Name: Group ID
Config.Description: Group-ID. Default 100 (users on Unraid).

Config.Name: Storage driver
Config.Description: How OpenCloud stores your files. Keep 'posix' (the default) for a normal local install - files live on the Data volume. Choose 'decomposeds3' ONLY to keep file blobs in an S3 bucket (then fill the five S3 fields below); even then the metadata tree stays on the local Data volume and must be backed up. Do NOT leave this blank and never type 'local' - both break file access (files appear but are greyed out and cannot be opened or downloaded). The driver is fixed at first start; to change it, start with a fresh Data folder.

Config.Name: S3 endpoint
Config.Description: S3 API endpoint URL. Self-hosted SeaweedFS: the internal http URL on its S3 port 8333, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:8333. Self-hosted Garage: its S3 API port 3900, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:3900. AWS/B2/Wasabi: their https endpoint. Only used when the driver above is 'decomposeds3'.

Config.Name: S3 region
Config.Description: Bucket region. Use 'default' for self-hosted SeaweedFS, 'garage' for self-hosted Garage (its default region), or your provider's region (e.g. eu-central-1) for AWS/B2/Wasabi. Only used with the 'decomposeds3' driver.

Config.Name: S3 access key
Config.Description: Access key ID for the bucket. Self-hosted SeaweedFS/Garage: the Access Key you set on that container's template directly. AWS: an IAM access key; B2/Wasabi: an application/API key.

Config.Name: S3 secret key
Config.Description: The secret that pairs with the access key. Self-hosted SeaweedFS/Garage: the Secret Key you set on that container's template directly. Stored masked.

Config.Name: S3 bucket
Config.Description: Name of the S3 bucket to store blobs in. Create it FIRST - the container does not. SeaweedFS: use its own 'Pre-create Bucket' template field. Garage: use its own 'Bucket' template field. Either way, or with any S3 tool. AWS/B2/Wasabi: create a bucket in the provider console. Enter that exact name here.

Config.Name: Web office suite
Config.Description: Browser document editing. 'off' (default) = none. 'collabora' = Collabora Online / CODE (port 9980); 'onlyoffice' = OnlyOffice Document Server; 'euro-office' = Euro Office, the sovereign OnlyOffice fork (image ghcr.io/euro-office/documentserver). The editor itself ALWAYS runs as a SEPARATE container that you install and point to below - this only turns on OpenCloud's built-in WOPI service and wires it up. For OnlyOffice and Euro Office the WOPI secret below MUST equal the document server's JWT secret. See the README 'Web office' section for the document-server setup and reverse-proxy notes.

Config.Name: Office document server URL
Config.Description: Browser-reachable URL of your Collabora / OnlyOffice document-server container, e.g. https://collabora.example.com (or http://192.168.1.10:9980 on a plain LAN). Only used when 'Web office suite' is not 'off'.

Config.Name: Office WOPI secret
Config.Description: A shared secret used to sign the WOPI tokens. Pick any long random string. REQUIRED for OnlyOffice and Euro Office and MUST be identical to the document server's own JWT secret field (JWT_SECRET / EURO_OFFICE_JWT_SECRET) - if it is left blank, documents open in read-only preview or fail with 'document security token is not correctly formed'. Not required for Collabora. Only used when 'Web office suite' is not 'off'.

Config.Name: Full-text search (Tika)
Config.Description: Search inside file CONTENTS (PDF, Word, Excel, ...), not just file names. 'false' (default) = OpenCloud's normal name/metadata search. 'true' = content search via Apache Tika. Tika ALWAYS runs as a SEPARATE container that you install and point to below: install a Tika template from Community Applications (search 'Tika'), image apache/tika, port 9998 (a '-full' tag also OCRs scanned images). NOTE: only files uploaded or changed AFTER you enable this are content-indexed; existing files are not re-indexed automatically (re-upload or edit them). See the README 'Full-text search' section.

Config.Name: Tika server URL
Config.Description: Network-reachable URL of your Apache Tika container, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:9998. Only used when 'Full-text search (Tika)' is 'true'.
